question: Should ClawHub establish an author-declared skill capability contract, and if so which vocabulary, authority model, and advisory-to-required rollout should become canonical?
rationale: This creates a public trust-boundary and compatibility contract that may later affect moderation and installation policy; repository evidence cannot safely choose those semantics.

options.title: Advisory canonical manifest
options.body: Define an optional shared schema, expose declaration-versus-observation discrepancies without blocking, preserve legacy skills, and evaluate adoption before enforcement.

options.title: Wait for upstream standard
options.body: Keep current metadata and coherence analysis until OpenClaw or AgentSkills adopts a shared capability vocabulary that ClawHub can consume.

options.title: Require new submissions
options.body: Select a schema now and require it for new skill versions while grandfathering legacy versions, accepting immediate publisher and moderation migration costs.

recommendation.title: Advisory canonical manifest
recommendation.body: Define an optional shared schema, expose declaration-versus-observation discrepancies without blocking, preserve legacy skills, and evaluate adoption before enforcement.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the closest prior implementation across all affected contract surfaces.
